result:
Typing alone does not select or notify anyone. When the comment is submitted, the typed `@handle` in its body is matched against organization members, and the resulting user IDs travel through the comment event to the notification service.

1. In [mention-query.ts](src/components/domain/comment/mention-query.ts), `mentionHandle` derives a member’s handle from the local part of their email; `matchMembers` supplies autocomplete suggestions and `applyMention` inserts the chosen handle into the text. In [mention-textarea.tsx](src/components/domain/comment/mention-textarea.tsx), `emit` calls `resolveMentions` from [mentions.ts](src/lib/mentions.ts), which extracts distinct handles from the body and maps handles that match organization members to user IDs. The parent [comment-composer.tsx](src/components/domain/comment/comment-composer.tsx) passes those IDs as `mentionedUserIds` when submitting.

2. The [create-comment.ts](src/actions/comments/create-comment.ts) Server Action validates and authorizes the request, then calls `createComment` in [comment-service.ts](src/server/services/comment-service.ts). That service loads up to 100 organization members and resolves the body again. It unions the server-resolved IDs with client-supplied IDs that belong to those loaded members, stores the result with the comment, then emits `comment.created` with `mentionedUserIds`.

3. The `comment.created` event type carries that ID list in [event.ts](src/types/event.ts). The event bus delivers it to the subscriber registered by [notification-service.ts](src/server/services/notification-service.ts), which [event-registry.ts](src/server/services/event-registry.ts) imports during server startup. For each ID, the subscriber calls `notify` with kind `comment_mention`. `notify` deduplicates recipients and skips the comment author.

4. For each remaining recipient, `notify` loads that person’s `comment_mention` preference and calls `resolveChannels`. With no saved preference, the default channels are `in_app` and `email`. With a preference, `inApp` controls the inbox channel; `email` controls email eligibility, while `digestOnly` suppresses immediate email unless the organization has the `digest_email` feature enabled. If no channels remain, `notify` skips the recipient entirely. Otherwise it calls `insertNotifications` in [notification-repository.ts](src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts), which stores one notification row with the chosen channels. That row is what appears in the recipient’s inbox; [inbox/page.tsx](src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/inbox/page.tsx) loads notifications for the signed-in user.

The delivery decision is stored as channel metadata on the row. In the code path traced here, the subscriber creates that row; it does not directly send an email.
